protocol.purpose: Current-size optimizer contrast and same-state CFG; convergence before capacity changes

auxiliary_classifier.purpose: fixed auxiliary evaluator of generated requested-class agreement
auxiliary_classifier.retention: one frozen evaluator and its compact training records until explicitly removed

protocol.preflight: 12 compiled BF16 plain-model steps, full real loader/holdout, intermediate and guided final generation
protocol.estimated_gpu_hours: 3–5 aggregate GPU-hours; approximately 1.5–2.5 hours at two GPUs, availability dependent

artifact_purposes.compiler_cache: Reproducible compilation and bounded cold-start overhead; at most 1.5 GiB expected
artifact_purposes.diagnostic_grids: One 100-image final EMA CFG1 grid per quality run; one 10-image preflight grid

protocol.retention: Declared evidence, diagnostic grids and compiler caches until explicitly removed; existing evaluators unchanged
protocol.ema: in-memory .999; intermediate and final evaluations before the process exits
limits: Two paired seeds on one held-out split; sample SD is not a confidence interval.
All recipes train with10% label dropout; this does not isolate dropout versus the historical no-dropout regime.
Beta1 changes use a fixed base and adapter LR; no update recalibration or quality-based rate selection.
Plain and DPLR use the same width/depth, not equal total parameters; capacity remains a confound.
Guidance scales are evaluated on the same EMA state/noise; scale1 uses one forward and other scales use two.
Intermediate quality uses CFG1 only; the final state evaluates all three scales.
FID is finite-sample 5k-image held-out-train FID, not published50k-image FID.
Classifier agreement is an auxiliary proxy; real accuracy and per-class confusion are retained.
Compilation is common to all recipes; throughput is concurrent and not an isolated speed experiment.
Thirty thousand steps are a convergence probe, not proof of saturation; larger models are deferred.

limitations: One fixed validation split; seed spread is not a confidence interval or test-set estimate.
FID uses held-out train images and finite sample counts; not published 50k-image FID.
Wrong-class loss measures sensitivity/use, not generated class accuracy.
External condition is a single class/time vector; sequence-conditioned cross-attention is not evaluated.
Concurrent throughput shares CPU/storage; matrix FLOPs omit non-matmul work and backward.
Generative evaluation time includes sampling and FID feature/statistic computation; isolated inference throughput is not measured.
Each screen has its own declared LR/initialization recipe; optimal rates are not established without bracketing.

limitations: One fixed validation split; seed spread is not a confidence interval or test-set estimate.
FID uses held-out train images and finite sample counts; not published 50k-image FID.
Wrong-class loss measures sensitivity/use, not generated class accuracy.
External condition is a single class/time vector; sequence-conditioned cross-attention is not evaluated.
Concurrent throughput shares CPU/storage; matrix FLOPs omit non-matmul work and backward.
Generative evaluation time includes sampling and FID feature/statistic computation; isolated inference throughput is not measured.
Each screen has its own declared LR/initialization recipe; optimal rates are not established without bracketing.
